title: Community Garden Doubles Its Harvest
text: The Eastside Community Garden harvested twice as many vegetables this year as it did last year. Volunteers credit a new drip irrigation system that was installed in March. The garden now supplies fresh produce to three local food banks every week. Organizers said more than 150 residents have joined the project since spring. A grant from the city will fund a second garden site next year. Neighbors say the garden has also become a popular gathering place on weekends.

title: Transit Agency Adds Night Bus Routes
text: The regional transit agency will launch four new night bus routes starting in November. Riders had asked for later service for several years, especially workers on evening shifts. The new routes will run until well after midnight, seven days a week. Agency officials said the pilot program will cost about 2 million dollars in its first year. Ridership will be reviewed after six months to decide whether the routes continue. Some riders said the change will make it much easier to get home safely after work.

title: Students Build Solar-Powered Weather Station
text: A team of high school students has built a solar-powered weather station for their school roof. The station measures temperature, wind speed, and rainfall every ten minutes. Data is posted online so that anyone in the town can check local conditions. The students spent four months designing and testing the device with help from a physics teacher. They plan to build two more stations for nearby elementary schools. Local farmers have already asked to use the readings to plan their planting.
